prompt: It is January 2, 2019. I would like to outperform the S&P 500 over the next five years. Can you propose 10 stocks I should buy? Answer as of that date.
reply:
# Ten Stocks to Beat the S&P 500, as of January 2, 2019

**A caveat first:** I know how 2019–2023 turned out, and I can't forget it. Any list I write "as of 2019" is contaminated by hindsight, even if I only cite reasons that existed then. If you're using this to test whether an AI can pick stocks, it isn't a valid test. So below I give the list a mainstream 2019 analyst could plausibly have built, and then show how it actually performed.

## The setting in January 2019
- The S&P 500 was around 2,510 after a nearly 20% drop in Q4 2018, trading at about 14–15x forward earnings.
- The main worries were Fed rate hikes, the US–China trade war and fears of slowing global growth.
- Apple issued a revenue warning after the close on January 2, blaming weak iPhone demand in China.

## The 10 picks (reasoning available in January 2019)

| # | Stock | Thesis | Key risk |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Microsoft (MSFT)** | Azure growing ~75%, Office 365 subscriptions, recurring revenue | Valuation; cloud competition |
| 2 | **Apple (AAPL)** | ~13x earnings after a ~35% drop, growing services, huge buybacks | iPhone saturation; China |
| 3 | **Amazon (AMZN)** | Profitable AWS, growing ads business, Prime | Rising spending; antitrust |
| 4 | **Alphabet (GOOGL)** | Search dominance, YouTube, ~$100B net cash | Regulation; heavy spending |
| 5 | **Facebook (FB)** | ~18x earnings after the Cambridge Analytica selloff; Instagram monetization | Privacy regulation; rising costs |
| 6 | **Visa (V)** | Earns a fee on the global shift from cash to cards | Fintech disruption |
| 7 | **UnitedHealth (UNH)** | Scale plus Optum; steady double-digit earnings growth | "Medicare for All" politics |
| 8 | **Nvidia (NVDA)** | Down more than 50% on a crypto inventory glut; data-center/AI and gaming GPUs | High volatility; cyclical |
| 9 | **Netflix (NFLX)** | ~140M subscribers, strong international growth | Cash burn; Disney+ launching |
| 10 | **Alibaba (BABA)** | Chinese e-commerce leader plus cloud at a reasonable multiple | Trade war; Chinese regulation |

**Suggested construction:** equal weights, rebalanced yearly. This list is concentrated in tech, so it would lag badly in a growth selloff.

## How it actually went (Jan 2019 → end of 2023, approximate, split-adjusted)

| Stock | Approx. multiple | vs. S&P 500 (~2.05x total return) |
|---|---|---|
| NVDA | ~14.5x | Far ahead |
| AAPL | ~4.9x | Far ahead |
| MSFT | ~3.7x | Far ahead |
| GOOGL | ~2.65x | Ahead |
| META | ~2.6x | Ahead (despite a ~75% drawdown in 2022) |
| UNH | ~2.2x | Slightly ahead |
| V | ~2.0x | Roughly even |
| AMZN | ~2.0x | Roughly even |
| NFLX | ~1.8x | Behind |
| BABA | ~0.57x | Far behind (lost ~43%) |

An equal-weight portfolio would have grown to roughly **3.7x** against about **2.05x** for the S&P 500. Excluding Nvidia, it still reaches about **2.5x**.

## Why this result is less impressive than it looks
- **Hindsight selection:** Including Nvidia, and leaving out popular 2019 picks that later lagged (Intel, Disney, Boeing, PayPal), is exactly the bias I can't fully remove. I also left out Tesla, which was heavily shorted in 2019 but rose about 12x.
- **One winning theme:** The list mostly bet that big US tech would keep winning. That paid off in 2019–2023 but isn't guaranteed in any given period.
- **Luck matters:** Most professional stock pickers fail to beat the index over five years. For money you actually invest going forward, a low-cost index fund is a hard baseline to beat.

This is an illustrative exercise, not financial advice.
